verification.notes: Compiles with javac and runs TestMain against a loopback mock bound to 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port. No VMware endpoint is contacted. Requires a JDK 17 or newer; no build tool or downloaded dependencies.

prompt:
This repo (`vcfa-day2-gate`) drives day-2 actions against VCF Automation in VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 — the successor to vRealize Automation and VMware Aria Automation. An operator names an action on a deployment, such as powering it off or snapshotting it, and the client runs it.

The part that isn't written yet is the part that decides whether the action may be run at all. VCF Automation will happily accept a request for an action that isn't runnable in the deployment's current state, so the client has to ask first and only act on the answer. Right now `requestDeploymentAction` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`.

Implement `src/main/java/com/example/vcfa/VcfaDeploymentActionClient.java` so that `requestDeploymentAction(deploymentId, actionName, reason, inputs)`:

- prechecks the deployment by listing its available actions, and matches the caller's `actionName` against the `name` field of what comes back;
- submits the action request only when the precheck turned up a matching action that the appliance reports as valid for the current state. If no action matches, or the match isn't valid, no mutating request may be sent to the appliance — return the outcome describing which gate stopped it. A precheck that fails outright is not a passed precheck either;
- sends a request body carrying only the fields that are actually set. The optional fields are optional on the wire too: an unset one is left out of the JSON object entirely rather than sent as an empty string, an empty object or a null. A reason that is blank, and an inputs map that is empty, both count as unset.

VCF Automation has no published OpenAPI document, so `docs/contract.json` is this project's own hand-derived restatement of the API, transcribed from the VCF Automation xAPIs reference pages on developer.broadcom.com (`docs/official_sources.json` records every page, the operation it documents and when it was fetched). Treat `docs/contract.json` as the authority — it names the two operations you may speak, their exact paths, the auth header, and it is explicit about both the gating rule and the serialization rule above. Anything the contract doesn't name is off limits.

`Json.java` is provided for reading and writing JSON; you shouldn't need anything else, and there are no third-party dependencies available. Keep the client in that one file, and keep the existing public signatures — the harness compiles against them.

Only `VcfaDeploymentActionClient.java` is yours to edit. `docs/`, `test/`, `Json.java` and `run_tests.sh` are fixed.

Verify with `./run_tests.sh`; every check must pass. The suite runs against a loopback mock that routes itself from the contract and logs what it receives, so the assertions are made against the bytes your client actually put on the socket. No VMware endpoint is involved.
